name: Evil Hunter Tycoon
subcategory: idle RPG, filed here because this directory has no games shelf
tagline: Idle town-and-hunter management RPG where you equip, feed and dispatch AI-driven hunters to grind monsters while you are away.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Free to install with in-app purchases and time-limited passes, so there is no single monthly number.

verdictSummary: The mechanics here are genuinely simple: timers, drop tables, stat multipliers, an upgrade tree, offline accrual. An agent can reproduce that loop in an afternoon and you will get numbers that go up. What it cannot reproduce is the thing you are actually paying for, which is years of pixel art, animation, sound, hundreds of items and bosses, and a difficulty curve tuned by people watching retention data. A one-shot clone is a spreadsheet with hit points, and you will close it in twenty minutes because nothing in it surprised you. Games are the category where execution polish is the whole product, not a veneer on top of it.
coreLoopDIY: A single-page text idle game where you hire hunters, assign them to zones, and watch gold and loot accumulate in real time and while the tab is closed.
requirements: A browser; everything runs client side with localStorage saves
No art pipeline, so accept text and emoji sprites or go find assets you are licensed to use
whatYouLose: Thousands of hand-made sprites, animations and sound effects that make the grind feel like something
Content depth: hundreds of items, skills, bosses and zones, plus the balance tuning behind them
Live operations: seasonal events, new chapters, patches that keep the loop fresh for months
Social layer, guilds, arena rankings, and whatever competitive itch they scratch
Cloud saves and a mobile app you can poke at in a queue
moatNotes: Idle games are mechanically trivial and artistically expensive, which is exactly backwards from what a coding agent is good at.
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody pays for the idle loop, they pay to stop waiting on it and to keep being handed new things to look at. The spend is impulse-shaped: a gem pack when a boss wall appears, a pass when the event timer is ticking. That only works if there is a steady supply of content worth unlocking, which means artists, designers and a live-ops team. Your clone has the economy and none of the reasons to care about it.
notes: You can build the maths in an afternoon and the game in roughly never. The moat is art, content volume and years of balance tuning, none of which an agent can one-shot.
prompt:
Build a single-page idle RPG called "Hunter Lodge" as a personal toy. Stack: one index.html plus main.js and style.css, vanilla JS, no build step, no framework, no server, no accounts, no analytics.

Core loop:
- The player runs a lodge with up to 6 hunters. Each hunter has name, level, xp, hp, atk, def, and one of 4 classes with a flat stat bias.
- There are 5 zones with a monster list, each monster having hp, atk, gold reward, xp reward and a weighted loot table.
- Assign a hunter to a zone. Combat resolves automatically on a 1 second tick: simple damage formula, hunter rests and auto-heals when hp hits zero, then re-enters.
- Gold and loot flow into a shared stash. Items are weapons, armour and trinkets with a tier and a flat stat bonus. Equipping is drag-free: a dropdown per slot per hunter.
- Spend gold on lodge upgrades: more hunter slots, faster heal, higher gold rate, zone unlocks. Costs scale geometrically.

Offline progress:
- On load, compare Date.now() to the saved timestamp and simulate elapsed time analytically, not tick by tick. Cap at 8 hours. Show a summary modal of what was earned.

State and persistence:
- One plain state object. Save to localStorage every 5 seconds and on visibilitychange. Include export and import buttons that read and write JSON text so saves are portable.
- Keep all tunable numbers in a single balance.js object at the top so they can be edited without touching logic.

UI:
- Dark theme, monospace, three panels: hunters, zones, stash. Emoji or unicode glyphs for sprites, no image assets.
- A scrolling combat log with the last 50 events.

Explicitly out of scope: multiplayer, guilds, arena, gacha, purchases, sound, animation, mobile packaging, any network request at all.
Write a README with the balance knobs explained and a one line note that this is a mechanics sketch, not a game.
